angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 384,026 km at 149.18 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.7035 +/- 0.0268 mas (same row, RUWE 0.94): 149.18 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.552 +/- 0.017 solar radii from Castro González et al. 2020, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-318 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020MNRAS.499.5416C/abstract): 384,026 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.561 +/- 0.05 solar masses from Castro González et al. 2020, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-318 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020MNRAS.499.5416C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3851 +/- 83 K from Castro González et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-318 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020MNRAS.499.5416C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Castro González et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-318 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020MNRAS.499.5416C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-318.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.703, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
